world.title: Police arrest Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan's sister in Lahore ahead of party's planned march
world.summary: Police arrested Aleema Khan, sister of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, at her home in Lahore, according to a spokesman for the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party. The arrest occurred on September 20, just days before a planned protest march by the party scheduled for September 27. The reasons for her arrest have not been disclosed.

world.title: Uttarakhand glaciers retreat 23m a year on average; some lose 88m: Study
world.summary: A study reveals Uttarakhand's glaciers are retreating at an average rate of 23.23 meters annually, with the Khatling Glacier retreating the fastest at 88 meters per year. The research, titled “Time-dependent assessment of glacier recession in the Indian Central Himalaya,” utilized satellite imagery and observations from 1990 to 2024, noting a rise of nearly 500 meters in equilibrium line altitude.

world.title: 'Largest-ever' attack: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia, oil refinery hit; 3 killed
world.summary: Ukraine launched over 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, marking the largest drone attack to date. Hundreds of drones targeted Moscow, and an oil refinery was struck. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the assault, which resulted in three fatalities. The attack highlights the ongoing conflict between Ukraine and Russia, escalating tensions in the region amid ongoing military operations.

business.title: Search continues for 6,000 people 4 weeks after Nepal floods
business.summary: Search efforts are ongoing for approximately 6,000 individuals missing four weeks after devastating floods in Nepal. The floods have caused significant destruction, displacing thousands and complicating rescue operations. Authorities are working tirelessly to locate those unaccounted for, while relief efforts continue to provide aid to affected communities. The situation remains critical as the search for survivors persists.

business.title: Gold price prediction: Will US-Iran war, crude oil rates impact yellow metal rates? Check technical outlook
business.summary: Gold prices are anticipated to remain volatile, influenced by fluctuations in Treasury yields, the US dollar, and inflation data. Traders will closely watch developments in the US-Iran conflict and crude oil prices, which may also impact gold rates. The market is expected to move within a range as these factors evolve in the coming week.

business.title: Tata Trusts denies any deadlock at September 17 Board meeting, disputes casting vote mandate
business.summary: Tata Trusts has denied any deadlock from the September 17 Board meeting and disputed the casting vote mandate. The Trusts challenged Tata Sons' reappointment of N. Chandrasekaran as chairman, declaring it void due to insufficient support from Nominee Directors. They argue that the Articles of Association necessitate affirmative backing from a majority of Trust representatives for such decisions.

technology.title: 50 Moves, 30 Minutes and No Humans: MIT robot builds and repairs its own science experiment
technology.summary: MIT researchers have created a robotic laboratory capable of independently assembling and aligning optics experiments. In a demonstration, the robot successfully built a functioning laser cavity in approximately 30 minutes and was able to restore its alignment after the setup was disturbed by researchers. This advancement showcases the potential for automation in scientific experimentation without human intervention.

technology.title: Don’t buy a $500 dumbphone. These apps will make your Android phone calm
technology.summary: A minimalist phone, or "dumbphone," can be appealing, but spending $500 may not be necessary. Instead, open-source, ad-free Android apps can transform devices like the Pixel 9a into calmer, less distracting tools. By focusing on essential functions such as calls, maps, and calendars, users can reduce distractions without the need for an expensive alternative.

technology.title: Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold review: A steady evolution sees flagship foldable focus on software
technology.summary: The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold focuses on enhancing software and AI rather than introducing significant hardware changes. While it is not a revolutionary upgrade, it includes a new feature called “App Handles,” allowing users to pin apps to the taskbar for flexible access. This feature, initially introduced with the Pixel Fold, aims to improve the overall user experience.

sports.title: Asian Games 2026: Full September 21 schedule, IST timings and Indians in action
sports.summary: The Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, will feature Indian athletes competing in 11 disciplines on September 21. Events include medal competitions in swimming, shooting, soft tennis, and wushu. The schedule outlines specific timings for each event involving Indian participants, highlighting the country's involvement in various sports during the ongoing multi-sport event.

sports.title: I want to focus on my batting - Nigar Sultana on her decision to quit T20I captaincy
sports.summary: Nigar Sultana announced her resignation as T20I captain to concentrate on her batting. Following Bangladesh's semi-final loss to India, she expressed confidence in securing a bronze medal at the Asian Games, which will be her final match in the captaincy role. Nigar had previously communicated her decision to the board, indicating her desire to step down after the tournament.

sports.title: I want to focus on my batting - Nigar Sultana on her decision to quit T20I captaincy
sports.summary: Nigar Sultana announced her decision to resign as T20I captain to concentrate on her batting. Following Bangladesh's semi-final loss to India, she expressed confidence in securing a bronze medal at the Asian Games, which will mark her final match in the captaincy role. Nigar had previously communicated her intentions to the board regarding her future leadership.

health.title: HIV Injections Outperform Daily Pills for Teens in African Trial: Study
health.summary: A clinical trial in Africa found that eight-weekly HIV injections are more effective than daily pills for adolescents. Published in The Lancet, the study reported a 1% viral rebound rate for injections compared to 6% for tablets. Researchers are advocating for broader access to this injectable treatment in low-resource settings to improve HIV management among teens.

health.title: HIV injections keep virus suppressed better than daily pills: Study
health.summary: A clinical trial in Africa found that eight-weekly HIV injections were more effective at keeping the virus suppressed than daily pills among adolescents. Researchers emphasized the need for broader access to this treatment in low- and middle-income countries. The study highlights the potential benefits of injectable therapies in managing HIV, particularly in populations with limited access to daily medication.

health.title: Chronic inflammation linked to silent heart damage, study says
health.summary: A study involving nearly 480,000 UK adults has found that chronic inflammation, associated with everyday stress, socioeconomic disadvantage, and lifestyle factors, may cause silent heart damage years before any cardiovascular symptoms manifest. This research highlights the potential long-term effects of inflammation on heart health, emphasizing the need for awareness regarding the underlying factors contributing to cardiovascular disease.

science.title: Roman telescope captures first test image - Live Science
science.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully captured its first test image using its 300-megapixel infrared camera. The image features hundreds of stars, which appear as greenish rings due to the camera's incomplete focus. Full scientific images from the telescope are anticipated to be released in early 2027, marking a significant milestone in astronomical observation.

science.title: A new tooth test suggests T. rex was not cold-blooded like modern reptiles; the giant predator’s body temperature was estimated at a human-like 97°F
science.summary: A recent study indicates that T. rex had a body temperature of approximately 97°F (36°C), suggesting it was warm-blooded rather than cold-blooded like modern reptiles. Researchers utilized unique tooth analysis to explore the dinosaur's physiology, revealing that T. rex was likely more active than previously believed. This finding challenges long-standing assumptions about the thermal regulation of large prehistoric predators.

science.title: In 2026, CT scans showed 3.7-million-year-old “Little Foot” had ape-like arm strength but human-like leg loading, suggesting a mix of climbing and upright walking
science.summary: A study of the 3.7-million-year-old Australopithecus skeleton known as "Little Foot" reveals a combination of ape-like arm strength and human-like leg structure. This unique anatomy suggests that early hominids were capable of both climbing and upright walking. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of human evolution and the locomotion of our ancient ancestors.

entertainment.title: 'Neem Karoli Baba's daughter has watched Hanuman Ansh 15 times and cried each time,' says producer Ragini Sona: 'We saw that she is a total replica of Baba'
entertainment.summary: Producer Ragini Sona reported that 'Hanuman Ansh' has earned over Rs 329.30 crore globally, attracting a diverse audience. Notably, Neem Karoli Baba's daughter has watched the film 15 times, expressing emotional responses each time. Sona emphasized the film's success is linked to the blessings of Neem Karoli Baba, highlighting the spiritual connection resonating with viewers.

entertainment.title: ‘She cried each time’: Neem Karoli Baba’s daughter watched Hanuman Ansh 15 times
entertainment.summary: Producer Ragini Sona discussed her meeting with Girija ji, the daughter of Neem Karoli Baba, before the release of the film "Hanuman Ansh." She recounted how Girija ji expressed her emotions after watching the film 15 times. Sona shared her inspiration from meeting Neem Karoli Baba at age six, while Vishal detailed his research and motivations for the project.

entertainment.title: Kangana Ranaut HITS BACK at people trolling Maithili Thakur for arriving in Rolls-Royce at Lalbaugcha Raja: 'Some people a**** start to burn'
entertainment.summary: Kangana Ranaut has defended Maithili Thakur, a young singer and Bihar MLA, after she faced online trolling for arriving at Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja pandal in a Rolls-Royce Cullinan. Ranaut questioned why some individuals react negatively when politicians engage in public events. Her comments highlight the ongoing discussion about public figures and their choices in transportation and appearances.
